n: Add-on part for launch bases and stands that provides a rotatable launch rail for angled launching of rockets. This is the Small size rail, meant for smaller rockets. n: The "Milkstool", as it was nicknamed, was a stand created to allow the Saturn IB-Apollo to use the Saturn V's Launch Umbilical Tower on LC 39. The three Skylab crews and the Apollo CSM for the Apollo-Soyuz Test Project were launched from LC 39 with the milkstool. In reality it was a gray color, but a red variant is also available as an alternative. Attach the milkstool to a bottom center node of a rocket, then attach the launcher base to the bottom node of the milkstool. The center ring at top has switchable hold-down arm support and node arrangements. There is a built-in decoupler for separating the milkstool from a rocket for liftoff.

n: Add-on part for launch bases and stands that provides a rotatable launch rail for angled launching of rockets. This is the Large size rail, meant for larger rockets of size 1.25m and up. Rockets are only surface-attached to the rail, and the rail has built-in a decoupler. The rail can also be switched between the default forward direction and reverse. Rotating the rail can be done with the B9PD switcher or optionally with Animated Attachment installed via the deploy limit slider animation. The Animated Attachment method requires that the rail or launch base/stand be the root part in order to move the attached rocket. The rail part however can not be the root part after rotation or it will not decouple from the rocket. The rail can be rotated 100 degrees in the forward direction or 20 degrees in the reverse direction.

n: Add-on part for launch bases and stands that provides a rotatable launch rail for angled launching of rockets. This is the Medium size rail, meant for larger rockets of size 0.937m and up. Rockets are only surface-attached to the rail, and the rail has built-in a decoupler. The rail can also be switched between the default forward direction and reverse. Rotating the rail can be done with the B9PD switcher or optionally with Animated Attachment installed via the deploy limit slider animation. The Animated Attachment method requires that the rail or launch base/stand be the root part in order to move the attached rocket. The rail part however can not be the root part after rotation or it will not decouple from the rocket. The rail can be rotated 100 degrees in the forward direction or 20 degrees in the reverse direction.
